notes: Historical Profile 0.16 and early Profile 0.18 observations are preserved. Current closure is about the reusable artifact-bound structured projection membrane and Commons production use of it, not dynamic maps or text. Python retains external file/JSON/Git/clock I/O, append-only document integrity validation, and bounded transport assembly.

reproducer.attemptedProgram: mncs 0.18; module commons.pressure.projection; materialize bounded external pressure material into a declared typed row and run a native query
reproducer.command: Review the pre-campaign PressureRegistry.query projection and compile the bounded lifecycle kernel
reproducer.expected: Before the generic artifact-bound projection membrane, Python selected widths, finite labels, nested record construction, and bounded sequence structure while constructing PressureQueryRow. The existing native query kernel was not the production read path.

requiredBehavior: Given a loaded compiler artifact, an exact compiler-issued composite identity, and bounded structured input, materialize the declared MNCS value using compiler-owned field, primitive, finite, nesting, and bound contracts. Commons production queries then use native lifecycle, verification-state, selector, and filtering semantics; platform filesystem and JSON I/O remain host boundaries.
summary: The old Profile 0.16 diagnosis overclaimed a need for dynamic JSON, maps, and unbounded text. Profile 0.18 already represented bounded records, finite lifecycle values, and typed query kernels. The precise gap was an artifact-bound generic boundary to materialize bounded external structured input into declared record values; Commons also needed its production query path to consume those values in native lifecycle and filter kernels.
title: Reusable bounded structured records had no compiler-owned host projection boundary
